answer.label: Written by
answer.authorDates: 1978–2020 · NBA shooting guard, Los Angeles Lakers
answer.sourceLine: Bryant wrote it himself. The sentence sits mid-paragraph in The Mamba Mentality: How I Play (MCD / Farrar, Straus and Giroux, 2018), in a short entry headed “KEEP IT REAL,” where he is describing how he stopped managing his image for the press. The popular one-line version is a genuine verbatim extract — it is only the surrounding paragraph that gets dropped.

source.heading: The source

docMeta.dd: The Mamba Mentality: How I Play
MCD / Farrar, Straus and Giroux, 23 October 2018

source.excerpt: When I was young, my mindset was image, image, image. I took that approach with the media. As I became more experienced I realized: No matter what, people are going to like you or not like you. So be authentic, and let them like you or not for who you actually are.
trail: The line is carried as a sourced quotation on Wikiquote’s Kobe Bryant page ↗, quoted inside its full original paragraph and cited to The Mamba Mentality: How I Play (2018), entry “KEEP IT REAL.” Wikiquote lists no “Misattributed” or “Disputed” section for Bryant, and Quote Investigator has no page on this quote.

The book is Bryant’s own. Kirkus Reviews ↗ records publisher MCD / Farrar, Straus and Giroux, publication on 23 October 2018, 208 pages and ISBN 978-0-374-20123-4, and describes its contents as “short, no-nonsense snippets” — the format the “KEEP IT REAL” passage takes.

The publisher’s own page ↗ lists the title as a 2018 MCD × FSG hardcover with photographs by Andrew D. Bernstein, and Wikipedia’s article on the book ↗ describes it as built from short titled pieces grouped under “Process” and “Craft.”

One limit worth stating plainly: no library holds a full-text-searchable scan of the book — it is absent from Internet Archive search-inside and from the Open Library record ↗ for the work — so the wording could not be re-checked against a page image. The attribution rests on Wikiquote’s sourced entry, which names the book and the entry within it.
source.excerptNote: The paragraph runs on past the famous sentence: Bryant goes on to say that from that point he kept his answers blunt and straightforward, mixed in humour and sarcasm, and believes fans and reporters came to appreciate the real him. Text as transcribed in the sourced entry at Wikiquote; the entry title is recorded there, but no page number.

author.heading: About Kobe Bryant
author.metaLine: 1978–2020 · NBA shooting guard · Los Angeles Lakers, 1996–2016
author.bio: Kobe Bean Bryant (born Philadelphia, 23 August 1978; died Calabasas, California, 26 January 2020) spent his entire twenty-season NBA career with the Los Angeles Lakers, winning five championships, the 2008 MVP award and eighteen All-Star selections. After retiring in 2016 he moved into writing and film, winning an Academy Award for the animated short Dear Basketball. The Mamba Mentality: How I Play, published in 2018, was his own account of how he prepared, practised and thought about the game — written in short, blunt entries rather than as a conventional memoir.

context.heading: Why he said it
lead: The sentence is usually posted as free-floating self-help. In the book it is nothing of the kind — it is a working note about handling reporters. Bryant sets it up by admitting that as a young player his mindset was “image, image, image,” and that he carried that approach into press conferences. The line about authenticity is what he concluded once he had been doing it long enough to see that the image management was buying him nothing.

What follows in the same paragraph is the practical consequence rather than the uplift: he says he started keeping his answers blunt and straightforward, mixed in humour and sarcasm, and thinks fans and reporters ended up preferring that. So the quote is advice about media strategy that happens to generalise — not a motivational aphorism that happens to be about the press.
context.detailsSummary: A note on how this one circulates
detailsBody: Searching the exact wording turns up almost nothing beyond Wikiquote itself and a syndicated “quote of the day” item — which is unusual for a famous-name quote, and a good sign. The lines that get fabricated are the ones that spread everywhere with no origin; this one has a stated origin and comparatively little spread.

The one thing that does go missing in circulation is the source. It is routinely captioned with a bare “— Kobe Bryant,” which invites the assumption that it came from a speech or an interview. It came from a book he wrote, and the book names the passage.
context.pull: It is a note about press conferences, not a poster.

sourcesVerified.claim: Wikiquote carries the full paragraph including "So be authentic, and let them like you or not for who you actually are" and cites it to The Mamba Mentality: How I Play (2018), entry "KEEP IT REAL." The page has only "Quotes" and "Quotes about Bryant" sections — no Misattributed or Disputed section.

The Mamba Mentality: How I Play is an autobiographical book by Kobe Bryant, published by MCD (Farrar, Straus and Giroux), publication date 23 October 2018, 208 pages, with photography and afterword by Andrew D. Bernstein, foreword by Pau Gasol and introduction by Phil Jackson; it is structured as short titled pieces grouped under sections including "Process" and "Craft."
The publisher's own page lists the book as "HARDCOVER, MCD × FSG, 2018", featuring photographs by Andrew D. Bernstein, with blurbs from Phil Jackson and Pau Gasol.

Kirkus Reviews records publisher MCD/Farrar, Straus and Giroux, publication date October 23, 2018, 208 pages, ISBN 978-0-374-20123-4, and describes the book as consisting of "short, no-nonsense snippets."

Kobe Bean Bryant was born 23 August 1978 in Philadelphia and died 26 January 2020 in Calabasas, California; he played twenty seasons as a shooting guard for the Los Angeles Lakers (1996–2016), won five NBA championships and the 2008 MVP award, was an 18-time All-Star, and won an Academy Award for the animated short Dear Basketball.

Open Library's catalogue record for the work lists The Mamba Mentality: How I Play by Kobe Bryant with Andrew D. Bernstein and Phil Jackson, Farrar, Straus & Giroux, first published 2018 — and shows no scanned/full-text copy available.
